item.title: Slipstream: nonlinear beam dynamics in PyTorch
item.description: arXiv:2611.32300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Slipstream is a PyTorch package for nonlinear beam dynamics in storage rings, linacs and photoinjectors. It provides CPU and GPU particle tracking, field-map injector models with space charge, and automatic differentiation along supported tracking paths. Comparisons with elegant, ASTRA, GPT and other codes assess accuracy and computational cost for nonlinear ring tracking, optics matching and photoinjectors. Ring tunes agree with elegant to $10^{-9}$. For the tested ring workloads with tens of thousands of particles, GPU tracking in float32 is hundreds of times faster than the single-threaded CPU implementations compared here. Automatic differentiation reduces the time for 24-parameter optics matching by an order of magnitude compared to finite differences. Using a high-brightness photo-injector as an example, final horizontal emittances agree with ASTRA to about 1% at 20 and 100pC and differ by $\approx$4% at 250pC. For $2^{18}$ macroparticles, Slipstream's faster default settings take 14s on an RTX 3050 GPU and give emittances within 2% of that of ASTRA. Additional tests examine coherent synchrotron radiation, dynamic aperture and resistive-wall impedance. The package was developed predominantly by AI coding assistants under human direction. These comparisons identify where its models, GPU execution and derivatives are useful for repeated simulations in scans, fits and optimisation.
item.dc:creator: J. K. Jones, A. D. Brynes, M. King, H. L. Owen, A. Pollard

item.title: Toward light-controlled transverse Wigner ordering in attosecond electron beams
item.description: arXiv:2611.32156v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Kinetic fluctuations and space-charge expansion hinder Wigner ordering in free-electron beams. Here we propose a laser-driven route toward transient, substrate-free Wigner ordering that combines photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM) attosecond bunching, synchronized magnetic focusing, and spatial preconditioning. Classical relaxation and zero-temperature fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo trap benchmarks show that sixfold order survives quantum fluctuations from 1 T to sub-Tesla fields, defining ultrafast preparation targets.
item.dc:creator: Yiming Pan, Jiapeng Yang, Hao Geng

item.title: High-energy electron-positron beam collisions with large-angle disruptions
item.description: arXiv:2608.10988v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We demonstrate that the beam and field dynamics in high-energy electron-positron collisions are governed by a new dimensionless parameter $\varepsilon$. In the high-disruption regime, particles are deflected transversely at angles of order $\varepsilon$ while simultaneously undergoing longitudinal deceleration which scales as $\varepsilon^2$, accompanied by the emergence of a longitudinal electric field with amplitude proportional to $\varepsilon$. We identify the large-angle disruptions ($\varepsilon \ge 1$) as a novel extreme regime in which transverse motion becomes strongly relativistic and the braking effect fully arrests, and subsequently reverses, beam propagation. Our theoretical model is in good agreement with three-dimensional electromagnetic particle-in-cell simulations. Existing beam-beam studies are valid only in the $\varepsilon \ll 1$ limit. For proposed plasma-based linear colliders operating in the quantum regime, notable beam-beam effects generate low-energy secondary particles whose $\varepsilon$ can approach unity; the collision dynamics and behavior of these particles may therefore require fully electromagnetic particle-in-cell simulations for accurate modeling.
item.dc:creator: W. Zhang, T. Grismayer, L. O. Silva

item.title: A European high-capacity 100 MeV-per-nucleon heavy-ion facility for electronics irradiation based at CERN: Conceptual Design Report
item.description: arXiv:2608.26369v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This proposal presents a conceptual design for a European high-energy heavy-ion facility dedicated to electronics radiation-effects testing, directly addressing the critical challenges of global beam time shortages and energy limitations in existing facilities. Aligned with the HORIZON-CL4-2026-SPACE-03-85 call under Horizon Europe's Cluster 4 (Digital, Industry, and Space), the facility will enhance European sovereignty in space technology by providing approximately 1,900 additional hours of high-energy heavy-ion beam time annually, an increase of about 50% in the total heavy-ion beam time currently available in Europe for single-event-effect testing, and by extending the accessible ion energy range up to 100 MeV/nucleon, significantly improving penetration capabilities for state-of-the-art electronics testing. The facility will leverage CERN's ion injector chain up to the Low Energy Ion Ring (LEIR) synchrotron, adding a second ion source, a dedicated slow-extraction system, a transfer line and a user experimental area. The project timeline includes a pre-technical-design (pre-TDR) phase and a technical design phase leading to a Technical Design Report (TDR), followed by infrastructure and hardware production, installation, commissioning, and user operations. Funding is envisaged through a collaborative framework involving CERN and the European Union, with the aim of ensuring sustainable deployment and long-term operational success.
item.dc:creator: Edgar Cristopher Cort\'es Garc\'ia, Ruben Garc\'ia Alia, Matthew Alexander Fraser, Maciej Slupecki, Andreas Waets, Markus Widorski

item.title: A multiscale composition method for tracking electron bunches from periodically nanostructured photocathodes
item.description: arXiv:2609.11844v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Nanoholes and other periodic structures on a photocathode can enhance emission by increasing optical absorption and concentrating light. The curvature of a nanohole also alters electron emission directions and the local accelerating field. For the injector considered here, resolving holes of 200 nm nominal width across a laser spot 0.87 mm in diameter is computationally not feasible. We propose a multiscale composition method for tracking electron bunches from nanostructured photocathodes through rf injectors using conventional beam dynamics codes. For a cathode patterned with a 41x41 array of nanoholes, the method reproduces the transverse phase space obtained by resolving every hole in WarpX. The projected emittances agree to within 0.1% in both planes. We then apply this method to calculate the dynamics of a 100 pC bunch in an rf photoinjector with solenoid focusing. For a flat cathode with smooth emission across the same laser spot, the central-slice emittances at 5 m are about 15% above the nominal thermal emittance. The predicted central-slice emittances for the nanostructured cathode exceed those for the flat cathode by 13% horizontally and 19% vertically. The vertical emittance in this slice is modestly larger than the horizontal. No periodic modulation is visible in the transverse phase-space projections of the whole bunch.
item.dc:creator: Dmitry Bazyl, Igor Zagorodnov
